archetypes.name: contract-boundaries
archetypes.rationale: The plan intentionally preserves design workflow semantics while deleting implement workflow semantics, creating high risk of boundary drift across shared scripts.
archetypes.prompt_body: Investigate whether the proposed edits cleanly separate implement behavior from design behavior in shared renderers, timing reports, run-params, and report-tokens code. Look for places where an implement-only deletion could accidentally remove design SIMPLE/HARD handling or where shared defaults could reintroduce implement workflow state. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: legacy-artifacts
archetypes.rationale: Historical ledgers, run-flags, timing JSON, and committed logs may still contain workflow data that the plan says must be ignored without migration.
archetypes.prompt_body: Check the plan against repo evidence for compatibility with old implement artifacts containing WORKFLOW_PATH, workflow ledger rows, timing-report workflow_path values, or report-token fixtures. Focus on whether every reader that could consume historical implement artifacts is explicitly covered and whether the proposed tests prove non-leakage. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: operator-surface
archetypes.rationale: Removing a visible Path/workflow concept affects CLI help, docs, final reports, errors, and user-facing report labels across many surfaces.
archetypes.prompt_body: Review user-facing and operator-facing surfaces for stale HARD/SIMPLE implement wording, confusing unknown workflow remnants, or mismatched section names after the proposed change. Compare scripts, markdown docs, final-report composition, report-token issue labels, and acceptance greps for consistency with the plan. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
